title: Private upgrade agent and orchestrated DB migration workflow
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement an upgrade agent and orchestration workflow for Redwood Private installations (VPC and on-prem) that reliably applies control-plane and runtime upgrades while coordinating potentially disruptive DB schema migrations. The goal is a safe, observable, and resumable workflow that supports staged rollouts (canary -> phased -> full), preflight compatibility checks, backups and point-in-time restore hooks, and deterministic rollback paths for both code and schema changes. This ticket focuses on the agent design, migration plan format, coordinator behavior, and integration points with existing rollout gates and LTS channel semantics.
acceptance_criteria: An upgrade-agent binary/proc that can be installed on customer nodes and started as a system service or sidecar
Agent communicates with the Private control plane over mTLS and accepts signed upgrade plans
Upgrade plans express: version pins, ordered steps, db migration scripts (idempotent), pre/post checks, and rollback commands
Coordinator can schedule a phased rollout across host groups and abort/rollback mid-rollout
DB migration step supports dry-run, backup creation (pgdump/Cinder snapshot), and a safe-apply mode with verification queries
End-to-end test demonstrates upgrade with schema change and successful rollback path in a staging air-gapped environment
Operational telemetry emitted for each step with structured events visible in Console (start/complete/failure/latency)
Design doc and runbook published; internal security review completed prior to GA
tasks: Design: agent RPC and plan spec (schema + steps + signatures)
PoC: agent that can start, fetch plan, and apply a non-destructive step
Migration runner: idempotent migration adapter (SQL + external scripts)
Backup integration: hooks for snapshot and verify restore path
Coordinator: phased rollout controller with group assignments and timers
Console integration: per-host progress view and per-step logs
Testing: chaos test for mid-rollout abort and automatic rollback
Docs & runbook: installation, emergency rollback, troubleshooting

risks: Irreversible DB schema changes during partial rollout could require long downtime if rollback is not carefully designed
Air-gapped/on-prem networks may have strict egress rules, complicating plan delivery and telemetry collection
Customers with heterogeneous environments (mixed k8s + VMs) increase complexity of group rollouts
Migration scripts authored by customers may not be idempotent or reversible; we need automation to detect risky patterns
mitigations: Require migration steps to declare reversibility and provide down-scripts where possible
Default to backup-first mode for any step that touches persistent state; verify backups before apply
Support offline plan import for air-gapped installs (signed artifact upload) and manual approval paths
Add linter/validator for SQL migrations and run fast dry-run checks against a synthetic dataset
notes: Design choice: agent (lightweight) + central coordinator allows staged rollouts and easier support for VMs; operator-only approach is better for k8s but misses non-k8s customers
We will adopt LTS channel semantics: each plan targets a specific runtime LTS channel; agents must validate compatibility table before applying
Plan signing: use ed25519 keys managed by control plane; agents verify signature and reject unknown key IDs
